themes.topic: Intel EMIB-T advanced packaging progress and adoption
themes.summary: Intel's EMIB-T advanced packaging is reportedly 50% cheaper than TSMC CoWoS, with mass production expected next year as yields exceed 90%, despite substrate yield bottlenecks. It has secured an AI ASIC project from MediaTek (likely Google TPU), and Broadcom and Meta are evaluating it, with Google expanding TPU orders and using EMIB due to TSMC CoWoS capacity constraints.

themes.topic: NVIDIA Rubin Ultra HBM despec due to supply constraints
themes.summary: NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra HBM despec, shifting from HBM4E 12Hi to HBM4 8Hi, is a strategy to produce more accelerators from limited HBM supply, as DRAM makers struggle to expand HBM capacity due to commodity DRAM shortages and TSMC's capacity expansion outstripping HBM supply.

mentions.text:
Put simply, the Rubin Ultra HBM despec is a supply issue. Not a demand issue.

I think as much additional HBM will be produced as the supply headroom freed up by the shift from 12Hi to 8Hi. It is not a problem at all.

themes.summary: DigiTimes reports that 2027 DRAM and HBM capacity is already fully booked, with NAND flash bookings also expected to fill, leading to an acute supply shortfall and elevated memory prices becoming the norm due to prioritization of CSPs and AI majors.
